standard.name: NFPA 92 / NFPA 92B (historical)
standard.title: Standard for Smoke Control Systems / Guide for Smoke Management Systems in Malls, Atria, and Large Areas
standard.note: NFPA 92B was withdrawn in 2011 and incorporated into NFPA 92. Calculations follow the algebraic methods retained in NFPA 92 Chapter 5 (SI units).
standard.edition_note: Formulas and guidance based on NFPA 92B-2009 and equivalent SI forms in later NFPA 92 editions.

plume_equations_SI.flame_height_note: NFPA 92 SI form of limiting elevation (approx. mean flame height). Some handbooks also use 0.235*Qc**(2/5); app uses 0.166 form.
plume_equations_SI.units: Qc in kW, z in m, m_dot in kg/s

plugholing.note: Maximum volumetric flow per inlet without plugholing. Gamma depends on inlet location and temperature ratio.

makeup_air.max_velocity_note: NFPA 92 / common practice: makeup air velocity should not exceed 1.02 m/s (200 fpm) in the vicinity of the fire or openings that could disrupt the plume. Higher velocities may be acceptable remote from the fire with engineering analysis.
makeup_air.recommended_location: Low level, remote from expected fire locations, distributed to avoid high-momentum jets into the plume.

exhaust_inlets.min_number_guidance: At least two inlets recommended for reliability; distribute to avoid plugholing and short-circuiting.

checklist_categories.title: 1. Project & Regulatory Data
items: Project name, location, and occupancy classification
Applicable edition of NFPA 92 (or local adoption of former 92B methods)
Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ) requirements and amendments
Building code references (IBC, NFPA 101, local codes)
Design basis document / smoke control narrative prepared
Design objectives clearly stated (smoke layer maintenance, tenability, ASET/RSET)

checklist_categories.title: 2. Geometry & Space Description
items: Large-volume space dimensions (length, width, height) – SI units
Floor area and volume of the atrium / mall / large space
Highest walking surface elevation relative to fire source
Cross-sectional area variation with height (if non-uniform)
Openings to adjacent spaces and communicating areas
Location and size of potential fire sources
Ceiling configuration and any draft curtains / smoke reservoirs

checklist_categories.title: 3. Design Fire Scenario
items: Design fire type selected (steady-state or t-squared growth)
Heat release rate (HRR) justified by fuel load / occupancy / test data
Convective fraction (Qc / Q) documented (typically 0.6–0.7)
Sprinkler effect considered (activation time, HRR reduction if applicable)
Fire location (centre, wall, corner, balcony spill) identified
Fuel package separation distances checked for secondary ignition

checklist_categories.title: 4. Smoke Layer Design Criteria
items: Design smoke layer interface height (z) above highest walking surface ≥ 1.83 m
Minimum smoke layer depth ≥ 20 % of floor-to-ceiling height or justified by analysis
Clear height for means of egress maintained for required ASET
Tenability criteria defined (temperature ≤ 60 °C, visibility ≥ 10 m at 1.83 m height)
Time to reach design interface height calculated (filling or steady exhaust)

checklist_categories.title: 5. Calculation Methods & Results
items: Algebraic equations (NFPA 92 Chapter 5 / former 92B) or approved zone / CFD model used
Axisymmetric / balcony spill / window plume equations applied correctly
Mass flow rate of smoke production at design interface height
Volumetric exhaust rate at smoke temperature
Number and capacity of exhaust inlets checked against plugholing limit
Smoke density / optical density estimated if required for tenability
Makeup air quantity (85–95 % of exhaust) and velocity ≤ 1.02 m/s verified
Hand calculations or spreadsheet verified independently

checklist_categories.title: 6. System Components & Equipment
items: Smoke exhaust fans rated for required temperature-time class (e.g. 300 °C / 1 h or higher)
Fan redundancy / standby capacity (N+1 or dual fans) considered
Ductwork and dampers suitable for smoke control temperatures and pressures
Exhaust inlet locations and sizes coordinated with architecture
Makeup air openings / supply fans sized and located to avoid plume disruption
Fire / smoke dampers and control dampers listed for the application

checklist_categories.title: 7. Controls, Detection & Activation
items: Automatic activation by smoke detection or sprinkler waterflow
Manual activation capability provided at Firefighters’ Smoke Control Station (FSCS)
Control sequence documented (exhaust start, makeup air, HVAC shutdown, dampers)
Interlocks with fire alarm system and elevators / stair pressurization if present
Status indication and override at FSCS
Power supply reliability (emergency power for smoke control equipment)

checklist_categories.title: 8. Testing, Commissioning & Documentation
items: Acceptance testing plan prepared per NFPA 92 Chapter 8
Component testing (fans, dampers, controls) completed
System-level performance testing (pressure, airflow, smoke layer if practical)
Documentation package complete (design calculations, drawings, sequences, test reports)
Periodic inspection, testing and maintenance schedule defined
Owner training and O&M manuals provided

checklist_categories.title: 9. Special Conditions & Coordination
items: Interaction with stairwell / elevator pressurization systems evaluated
Opposed airflow method applied where communicating spaces require it
Natural venting (if used) supported by analysis or scale modelling
Stratification risk assessed (high ceilings, low HRR)
Wind effects and outdoor design temperatures considered for makeup air
Coordination with architectural features (glass, openings, balconies)

checklist_categories.title: 10. Acceptance Testing & Commissioning
items: Design documents include acceptance testing procedures and pass/fail criteria
Preliminary building inspection completed (construction status, openings, barriers)
Component testing completed for fans, dampers, detectors, controls, doors
Individual component capacities and functions verified
Complete smoke-control sequence demonstrated (normal → automatic smoke mode → standby power if provided → return to normal)
Airflow quantities measured at exhaust and makeup-air locations
Pressure differences measured across smoke barriers / openings as applicable
Door-opening forces verified where pressurization is used
Activation from automatic detection and manual means confirmed
Firefighter’s Smoke Control Station (FSCS) override and status indication verified
Testing performed under both normal and emergency/standby power (if provided)
Special inspector (where required by IBC/local code) present and report prepared
Final acceptance test report filed with AHJ and copy retained in building

checklist_categories.title: 11. Periodic ITM & Documentation
items: Dedicated smoke control systems tested at least semiannually
Non-dedicated systems tested at least annually
Airflow quantities measured at exhaust equipment and makeup-air supplies
Pressure differences measured at smoke barrier openings
Full control sequence operated for each design scenario
Results documented in O&M log and available for inspection
Equipment maintained per manufacturer recommendations
Any modifications re-tested and documentation updated
Detailed Design Report prepared (purpose, objectives, approach, assumptions, calculations, equipment specs, activation method, operation logic, commissioning procedures)
Operations & Maintenance Manual provided to owner (commissioning results, ITM frequencies, critical design assumptions, system purpose)
As-built drawings and control sequences current
Acceptance test report retained on site
